mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary cycle that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden rise in the federal funds rate above 4.0% signals aggressive monetary tightening, raising borrowing costs and dampening equity valuations, which predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p < 0.05) during periods when FEDFUNDS crosses above 4.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in the federal funds rate and growth in quarterly GDP (GDPC1) indicates an easing cycle combined with robust demand, creating a favorable environment for equity valuations and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p < 0.05) when both FEDFUNDS is below 4.0% and GDPC1 exceeds 16000.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime, a rise in the federal funds rate above 4.0% signals potential peak inflation concerns, leading to market uncertainty and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in late-cycle expansion periods with FEDFUNDS >4.0% are not significantly negative (t-test p >0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the INDPRO index above its 10-year average reflects robust supply-side growth, boosting corporate profits and consumer spending, which drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p <0.05) when INDPRO exceeds its 10-year average.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in UNRATE above 5.5% indicates weakening labor market conditions, raising long-term interest rates and reducing corporate profitability, which predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p >0.05) during UNRATE periods above 5.5%.

mechanism_narrative: Conflicting signals between falling federal funds rates (easing) and rising unemployment rates (UNRATE) create market uncertainty, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p <0.05) when FEDFUNDS <3.0% and UNRATE >5.0%.

mechanism_narrative: In a post-shock recovery regime, a rise in the federal funds rate above 3.5% is interpreted as cautious normalization, which supports equity valuations and predicts positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns in post-shock recovery periods with FEDFUNDS >3.5% are not significantly positive (t-test p >0.05).
